behavior: A host whose endpoints hang no longer holds its RPC role: when one endpoint of a host times out or can't connect, the whole host rests, so calls reach the role's next host
acceptance: When an endpoint times out or fails to connect, every endpoint of its host rests with it (the same rest and failure count), so a call reaches the role's next host after one AttemptTimeout instead of cycling through the host's other keys
A failure of one key (HTTP 401 or a rate limit) still rests only that key

Tests: three hanging endpoints of one host in front of a working host give the answer from the working host within about one AttemptTimeout; a startup with two enabled chains skips the unreachable one and still checks the other; no factory code on the first RPC stops even when the second shows code
docs/backend/architecture.md: the startup intro no longer says every failed check stops the process, and Running the loop says a host that hangs rests as a whole; unit passes
